en: Chan Master Xue’an Congjin’s Collection of Verses on Ancient Cases:
A Woman Emerging from Samādhi:
Who is there by the painted tower to the west? Meeting, they speak and laugh softly. The spring colors deepen as she reaches home; Flowers fall and the partridges cry.
Śāriputra entered the city and saw from afar the girl Candrottarā emerging;

not a single speck of dust rose from the great earth. She faced south and gazed at the Big Dipper. As the saying goes: "When a hen marries, she flies after the hen; when a dog marries, it runs after the dog."
In the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, the Buddha said to Ānanda: "When the seeing sees, that seeing is not [the ordinary] seeing;
seeing is already detached from seeing, such that seeing cannot reach it.
It is like seeing the horn of an ox over a wall and then mounting the ox; having mounted it, one rides into the bustling marketplace of red dust, wandering everywhere until returning to the stall.
Lying down, he vanishes in the dead of night; from before Kāśyapa’s gate, the banner-pole passes through every household door into Chang’an.
Not a hair’s breadth is seen, yet the field of vision is vast. No Dharma, no person—whom shall it be entrusted to?
Ting! Elder brother and younger brother mock each other.

When the Venerable Siṃha went to Kaśmīra, who saw the King of Dharma as empty space? Seeing his very essence, how could it ever be obstructed by the flash of a sword? In ancient temples, creeping vines pierce through the doors.
A window. A broken stele, shattered by wind and rain, its inscriptions still legible.

When Bodhidharma saw Emperor Wu of Liang, he stepped upon the earth-axis, yet the earth did not move; he pushed down the celestial gate, yet the heavens grew even higher. He sailed steadily in his iron boat back to the land of Shao.
The room remains, yet to this day the world continues to give rise to wind and waves.
Bodhidharma returned to the West with a single shoe;
after nine years of cold sitting, he had already failed. Returning to the West with a single shoe was merely another fabrication; the descendants of later generations are empty and deluded.
Imagination: the partridge cries not because of the spring breeze.
The Second Patriarch’s “settling the mind” was something he could never find. A faceless countenance turns crimson; turning over, he takes a tumble. With both hands, he gropes at empty space.
The Sixth Patriarch was asked by a monk, "Who shall obtain the robe and bowl of Huangmei? The Patriarch replied, "He who understands the Buddha-dharma shall obtain them.
The monk said, "Will you yourself, Master, obtain them? The Patriarch said, "I shall not obtain them. The monk asked, "Why not?
The Patriarch replied, "Because I do not understand the Buddha-dharma."
The Huangmei Buddha-dharma is not something that can be grasped; in dreams, one’s eyes are closed yet one remains alert. There is not even two taels of gold in this place;
the common man sells three sheng of wine.
National Teacher Zhong called his attendant three times.
A single arrow shot down two cranes; the two cranes fell as soon as they were struck by hand. The waves ripple against the city of Yueyang;
the moon fills the Tengwang Pavilion. Mazu said: "Since the time of chaos thirty years ago, I have never lacked salt or sauce to eat.
In those days, Gaojia had already passed the imperial examinations and read every ten thousand scrolls of books in the world; today, his entire being is one with heaven and earth.
[Nanquan] said, "It is narrow. It is better not to contemplate good things at all.
Baizhang said, "In the past, when I was struck by Mazu’s single shout, my ears were deaf and my eyes went black for three days straight."
A single shout strikes the head like a rushing thunderclap; even human speech before it would darken the soul. It seems this was not merely deafening for three days;
until this very day, the seas and mountains remain shrouded in gloom.
Nanquan said: "Mazu says, 'This very mind is Buddha. I, Old Master Wang, do not speak thus. I say:
'It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing. Is there any fault in speaking thus? When one shaves one's head, the head shines;
when one washes one's feet, the feet are refreshed. One takes off one's clothes and goes to bed to sleep; scratching, one reaches the itch all over the body."
Jiashan said: "When I was first at Damei, I lost one eye.
A bamboo fence and thatch hut; a wine flag slanting. A single gourd ruins both houses. After drinking, one knows not heaven from earth.
Returning, the ground is covered with peach blossoms."
As Panshan was about to pass away, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Is there anyone who has captured my true likeness?
They presented the portraits they had painted, but none met with the Master's approval. Puhua stepped forward and said, "I have captured it.
The Master asked, "Why do you not present it to this old monk? Puhua then performed a somersault and left. The Master said, "This..."
Han Xiang later pulled back the wind-crazed one;
in the thorough ice-pitcher, there is no reflection. Turning somersaults upside down, it is difficult to achieve through grasping.
After the rains have ceased on the thousand peaks following the Yellow Plum season, the moon of cassia rises once more from the sea.
Lu Zu faced the wall;
the Eyeless Immortal felt the bones. In the dark, groping about, they recognized kings and lords.
Though the price was high, in the end no one bought it. The stall has grown cold; desist in your idle chatter.
When Yaoshan built a hut for Shitou, he said, "It must not be like this;
it must not be like that at all. Stripping off his cloth robe until he was bare-boned, he struck him once right on the head.
Suddenly turning over, Shitou saw his mouth open and his eyes turn white.
People of the time saw this single stalk of flowers as if it were a dream;
root and trunk being of one substance, all was like a dream. Within the dream, the eyes are wide awake, yet there are flowers. A butterfly flies over the wall;
one knows not whose house the spring colors have entered.
Ganqi served congee;
Ganqi served congee. Nanquan smashed the cauldron. A common ailment, a thoroughgoing confusion. There is something even more laughable:
tomorrow morning they will starve the Chan monks to death.
Nanquan said: "The ordinary mind is the Way.
Once one awakens to this ordinariness, one reaches one's native home. Yet most people of the time fear falling into the ordinary.
Youth lasts but ninety days; even in total intoxication, there cannot be a hundred bouts.
Zhaozhou said: "This old monk employs the twelve-hour bell to usher in dusk and the rooster to announce dawn. Why trouble yourself with such vexations? Tear open the void into two sides;
from the incense burner of the ancient temple, a *zhicao* fungus emerges."
When Zhaozhou traveled on pilgrimage to Linji,
and Linji met Zhaozhou— both being patriarchs revered throughout the Chan forests— their encounter was like a sudden clash in a wrestling match.
Yet when meeting such practitioners today, they are merely called "two idle monks."
The secret demon’s wooden pitchfork is majestic and awe-inspiring, brooking no climbing upon it; yet once one leaps into its embrace, its face breaks into a smile.
Were it not for a capacity for wine as vast as the sea, who could know that the courage of his verse is as great as a mountain?
At Jeta’s Grove, he subdued the Māras;
with neither Māra nor self, the subduing was complete. This merely adds flowers to the eyes of people of this age. Today, the sword Mohe is of no use;
one knows well that a thief does not strike a poor house.
Linji ascended the hall. A monk stepped forward; the Master immediately shouted. The monk also shouted, then bowed. The Master struck him.
"Those with eyes on the tip of the staff lack sinews in their eyes. They often encounter turbid wealth; they rarely meet with pure poverty. Since entering the mountain gate—
The smoke-lock is severed; one knows not how many springs have passed upon the world.
Zhaozhou asked Chan Master Datong, "What is it like when one who has died the great death comes back to life?
The Master said, "Night travel is not permitted; you must arrive by the break of dawn."
Before the stage, at midnight, they manipulate puppets; their movements and dignified bearing are complete in every gesture.
Yet, when one reflects carefully, there is no logic in it—there must ultimately be someone pulling them from within.
Regarding the exchange between Xinghua and Mindé concerning one shout and two shouts:
the entire mechanism appears and vanishes; guest and host are clearly distinguished. Yet, it cannot be avoided that both were blind. Feeling for a turtle in the dead of night;
the bright moon shines upon accumulated snow.
When Xinghua saw a fellow practitioner arrive, as soon as he stepped onto the Dharma Hall, he let out a shout. The monk also shouted;

Mount Sumeru toppled over, and the waters of the sea flowed backward. Fellow practitioners visiting one another create nothing but enmity. Enough, enough! Tomorrow the yellow chrysanthemums will make even the butterflies sorrowful.
Yantou. Once, when a monk asked, "What is it like when the ancient sail is not yet raised? the Master said: "The donkey in the back garden eats grass.
When the ancient sail is not yet raised, the donkey in the back garden eats grass. The days are short and the nights are long; the traveler must hurry."
Qianfeng’s single path to the gate of nirvāṇa is not a blind throw in the face of reality; responding to capacity, he speaks directly. Qianfeng and Yunmen—two mouths with but one tongue.
If one is a person who continues the "fox-fur" tradition, their cleverness will turn into clumsiness.
Yunmen, while ascending the hall, said: "Hear the sound and awaken to the Way; see the form and clarify the mind. He then raised his hand and said:
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys some sesame cakes with money; letting go of his hand, he says, "So it was just steamed buns!
This suddenly transcends the phrase "seeing forms and hearing sounds," and does not involve the talk of "clarifying the mind and awakening to the Way. Flowers fall and birds sing beneath the crags.
At the temple, when the moon was bright, people called for a ferryman.
Heishan knew how to beat the drum;
Dangyang struck the drum of Fan-nan. The myriad phenomena and all living beings heard it standing right where they were. Had it not been so, everyone would not have been in unison.
The play is difficult to finish as the day wanes toward evening.
*Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. Once, a monk asked about the great matter of birth and death, requesting the Master to save him. The Master said:
"I lost my boat in Lake Dongting."
The boat is lost within Lake Dongting; the barefoot Persian sleeps beneath the waters. Though all the people of the world call out to him, he cannot be roused;
the spring breeze blows him into the village of apricot blossoms.
Regarding Huanglong’s Three Barriers:
"What is my hand like compared to the Buddha’s hand? Joining palms and facing south, one gazes at the Big Dipper.
The hare pushes the bright moon up the thousand peaks, drawing forth a smile from the cold mountain."
My feet are like those of a donkey; I hasten home as the sun is setting. Since ancient times, Chang'an has been as level as a mirror;
for no reason at all, I have stumbled drunk upon the yellow brocade.
Every person has their own karmic affinity; it is neither from this land nor from the Western Heaven. Striking the coral tree, every branch is beautiful;
scattering mercury beads, every grain is perfectly round.

The Buddha’s hands and the donkey’s feet arise from conditions. A Persian from the South Sea sails upon an iron ship; fine gold and beautiful jade are piled in heaps for sale, yet in the end, they have never been worth a single coin.
Wuzu Yan said: "The Double Soul of the Maidens: which one is the real?
The southern branch faces the warmth while the northern branch suffers the cold. For what reason does the spring breeze act in two different ways? Relying on the high tower, do not blow the flute;
let everyone remain there to gaze over the railing."
